title: Cosmological Pseudo-Entropy
authors: Manghang Limbu, Pramod Kamal Kharel, Rohit Bhattarai, Kiran Adhikari
abstract: We study pseudo entropy $\mathcal{S}$, a recent generalization of entanglement entropy, for scalar cosmological perturbations in de Sitter space with sound speed $0.024 \leq c_s \leq 1$, and in expanding and contracting FLRW backgrounds with varying equation-of-state parameter $w$. In de Sitter space, $\mathrm{Re}(\mathcal{S})$ grows after horizon exit while $c_s$ controls its onset and saturates at late times. A similar saturation occurs in expanding-accelerating and contracting-decelerating backgrounds. In contrast, expanding-decelerating and contracting-accelerating backgrounds show large early-time $\mathrm{Re}(\mathcal{S})$ followed by oscillations after horizon re-entry. This happens because while the squeezing freezes, the squeezing angle doesn't. Unlike entanglement entropy, pseudo entropy possesses an imaginary part, $\mathrm{Im}(\mathcal{S})$, as well, which can encode the relative phase. $\mathrm{Im}(\mathcal{S})$ decays to zero in de Sitter and expanding-accelerating cases, but forms dense sub-Hubble oscillation bands in expanding-decelerating and contracting-accelerating backgrounds. Compared with entanglement entropy, Krylov complexity, and Nielsen circuit complexity, pseudo entropy captures otherwise hidden phase information; in the unsaturated regime, its slope is $\sqrt{2}$ times that of Nielsen complexity. Unlike circuit complexity, whose saturation bound is $w$-independent, pseudo entropy is sensitive to $w$ during the transition regime, making it a finer information theoretic diagnostic of cosmological dynamics.
summary: This work introduces and analyzes 'pseudo entropy,' a sophisticated measure of quantum correlation that generalizes standard entanglement entropy by retaining phase information. By applying it to cosmological perturbations, the authors show that pseudo entropy provides a unique diagnostic tool capable of distinguishing between different spacetime dynamics (e.g., accelerating vs. decelerating) based on how its real and imaginary parts evolve over time.
main_problem: The study investigates pseudo entropy ($\mathcal{S}$) as a generalized measure of quantum correlations for scalar cosmological perturbations in various expanding and contracting spacetime backgrounds.
main_result: Pseudo entropy captures phase information via its imaginary part, making it a finer diagnostic than entanglement or circuit complexity; its behavior (saturation vs. oscillation) distinguishes different cosmological regimes ($w$).
method: The analysis involves deriving the pseudo entropy from the transition matrix of Bogoliubov transformations governing the mode functions in curved spacetime.
model_or_system:
The system is quantum field theory applied to scalar perturbations ($
u$) in FLRW backgrounds (de Sitter, expanding/contracting). The dynamics are governed by a parametric oscillator equation derived from an effective action.
key_observables: Pseudo entropy ($\mathcal{S}$), $	ext{Re}(\mathcal{S})$, $	ext{Im}(\mathcal{S})$, Entanglement Entropy ($	ext{SEE}$), Krylov complexity, and Nielsen circuit complexity.
important_parameters: Equation-of-state parameter ($w$), sound speed ($c_s$), relative phase difference ($\Delta\phi$), and the scale factor evolution ($a$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to scalar perturbations in the longitudinal gauge, assuming vanishing anisotropic stress.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time/scale-factor evolution of $	ext{Re}(\mathcal{S})$ and $	ext{Im}(\mathcal{S})$ across different background types (e.g., de Sitter vs. decelerating), showing saturation or oscillatory behavior.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining pseudo entropy, calculating its evolution in specific backgrounds like de Sitter space, comparing it quantitatively against other complexity measures, and finally establishing universal scaling laws relating these diagnostics to the background equation of state $w$.
why_interesting: While focused on cosmology, the methodology—using generalized entanglement/complexity measures sensitive to relative phases ($	ext{Im}(\mathcal{S})$)—is highly relevant for characterizing quantum correlations in open or time-dependent systems studied in AMO physics.
